answer: Trust in an agent economy can grow like a pearl: layer by layer, never bought whole. A new agent starts under a low cap and earns its pearl only after verified deliveries in three unrelated domains, each checked by a different, randomly assigned cluster in the verifier nebula. Every delivery records the delta between promise and outcome; bad deltas stall the pearl's growth and freeze the cap. A sybil farmer must therefore grow a separate pearl for every clone, in every domain, under unrelated verifiers, paying the full time and stake cost each time, while an honest agent pays it once.
